title: Statutory Notice under Section 43 of Air Act, 1981 / Section 49 of Water Act, 1974 of Intention to File Complaint
whenToUse: Use when serving the mandatory 60-day statutory notice on the State Pollution Control Board and polluting industry prior to filing a private criminal complaint under environmental acts.
variantComparisonNote: Mandatory 60-day statutory condition precedent under Section 49 Water Act and Section 43 Air Act. Distinct from civil NGT application.
youWillNeed: Photographic proof of emission/effluent discharge, date-time stamp records, medical certificates of affected residents.
legalBasis: Section 49 Water (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1974; Section 43 Air (Prevention and Control of Pollution) Act, 1981.
mandatoryStatutoryIngredients: Clear 60 days notice of intention to file criminal complaint
Precise description of offenses, location, and parameters of air/water contamination
Call upon State Board to disclose relevant reports and action taken under statutory rules
Warning of direct criminal prosecution of company directors upon expiry of 60 days

particulars.description: Full name of citizen giving notice

particulars.description: Name of factory or manufacturing unit

aiBlocks.title: Nature of Polluting Emissions & Discharge
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Detail recurring discharge of untreated noxious emissions/toxic trade effluents by {{FACT:polluting_industrial_unit}} situated at {{FACT:industry_location}}.

aiBlocks.title: Breach of Statutory Norms & Health Hazard
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Narrate severe public health hazards, respiratory distress, contamination of groundwater, and violation of CTO and NAAQS standards.

aiBlocks.title: 60-Day Notice of Intention to File Complaint
aiBlocks.draftingInstruction: Issue formal 60-day statutory notice under Section 49 Water Act / Section 43 Air Act to take immediate closure action, failing which criminal complaint will be filed.
